# Bot selection of upgrades are slower

## Problem statement

When the attract/demo bot is presented with the hold-full upgrade selection
overlay it picks an option after only **900 ms** (`BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS`),
so a viewer has no real chance to read the three offers before the bot has
already chosen — and once it chooses, the choice screen is torn down and only
the 3-2-1 countdown numeral remains, so nothing on screen says **which** item
the bot took. The bot's upgrade picks should dwell long enough to be watched
and should be visible on the countdown.

## Users

- **Attract/demo viewer** (the player watching the menu's 👁 Watch Demo
  attract run, or an idle-menu session): *"As a viewer of attract mode, I want
  to see the bot's upgrade options for a couple of seconds and then see which
  one it picked while the countdown plays, so the demo reads as a deliberate
  choice rather than an instant flicker."*
- **Player (human selection, incidental):** *"As a player, once I choose an
  upgrade I want to be reminded which one I took while the 3-2-1 countdown
  runs."* — the shared overlay tears its choice UI down on selection, so the
  chosen title is the only record during the countdown.
- **Designer / producer:** *"As a designer, I want the bot's overlay dwell to
  be one named, tunable constant so I can pace the demo without hunting magic
  numbers."*

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — **Bot dwell is 2.5 s.** In demo/attract mode the hold-full upgrade
  selection overlay (`MineralChoiceScene`) auto-selects only after a **2500 ms**
  pause, sourced from one named constant (`BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS` in
  `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts`, raised from 900); the bot therefore visibly shows
  the offered upgrades before choosing. Normal (non-demo) play still waits for a
  real pointer/keyboard selection and never auto-selects.
- AC2 — **Selected title under the countdown.** From the moment an option is
  selected until the countdown completes, the overlay renders the **chosen
  option's title** (its catalogue name, e.g. `Spread Shot Lv.3`) beneath the
  large 3-2-1 countdown numeral, and the title text is **destroyed** when the
  countdown finishes and the overlay closes — no title text, text object or
  tween outlives the overlay, and a fresh hold-full starts with no stale title.
- AC3 — **Countdown and resume are unchanged.** The selection still drives the
  existing beat-locked 3-2-1 countdown (2250 ms at the default 80 BPM) with its
  rising cue, the reduced-volume ghost fire still runs underneath, and the
  choice is still applied on the beat after "1" with the launcher's beat clock
  re-based. The title is purely additive presentation and never delays or
  alters selection, application or resume timing.
- AC4 — **Scope contained.** The mini-boss reward wheel's demo auto-spin delay
  is **not** changed by AC1 (it keeps its current separate delay/constant), and
  no other surface's timing changes; every gym that launches the shared overlay
  keeps its existing behaviour (no `autoSelectMs` passed) apart from gaining the
  title readout.
- AC5 — **Tests.** Unit tests in `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts`
  cover: the chosen title is exposed and rendered while the countdown runs, and
  is gone (`null`) after the countdown completes; a manual selection shows its
  own title; the constant-pinned bot dwell is asserted (auto-select does not
  fire before 2500 ms and does fire after it). The demo integration test
  (`src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts`) still asserts the
  selection → countdown → resume path and asserts the selected title is visible
  during the countdown. All existing overlay, gym-parity and countdown tests
  stay green.
- AC6 — **Docs.** `README.md` (attract/demo mode section) and
  `docs/Game Design Document.md` (§4.4 auto-select bullet and §4.5
  beat-locked-countdown bullet) are updated to state the **2.5 s** bot dwell
  and the selected title shown under the countdown (and removed with it).
- AC7 — **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes,
  including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site
  entries.**
- AC8 — **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Impact

A viewer of the attract-mode demo now gets a clear 2.5-second look at the bot's
three upgrade offers and can see exactly which one it took while the countdown
plays, instead of a near-instant pick that left no trace of the choice.

## Constraints

- Demo-only for the dwell: normal play must not gain any auto-selection
  (existing AC5 of AH-0MUXXQ1MN002RXGB must stay true).
- Tunables live in one shared place (`src/ai/botHumanLike.ts`), never as
  scattered magic numbers.
- The overlay keeps its single `onSelect` contract; it must not reach back into
  `PlayScene` by scene key.
- The countdown stays beat-derived (`createHoldFullCountdown` /
  `beatPeriodMs`), never a hard-coded 2250 ms.
- Headless test harnesses collapse text metrics to 0, so any title layout must
  keep a measurable fallback (mirroring the existing `CHOICE_*_LINE_HEIGHT`
  constants) and stay inside the 960 × 720 playfield.
- The overlay is shared by `PlayScene`, `HexMapScene`, `GymFormationScene`,
  `GymWeaponLeveling` and `GymPowerUpLeveling`; the title addition must keep
  gym↔game parity (no per-scene copies).

## Existing state

- `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts` exports `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS = 900` — the
  demo dwell used for the hold-full choice auto-select, the mini-boss
  hold-full-style fallback choice, **and** the mini-boss wheel auto-spin
  (`PlayScene.openMiniBossReward` → `autoSpinMs`).
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` (`init` → `autoSelectMs` /
  `autoSelectIndex`, `create` → `this.time.delayedCall`) auto-selects on the
  demo path. `select(index)` records the pending selection, tears down the
  whole choice UI (backdrop, heading, option labels/descriptions/details, the
  `★ New` badges, the `YOUR UPGRADES` panel, the keydown handler) and draws the
  large countdown numeral at `COUNTDOWN_Y = 270` (96 px, neon cyan).
  `completeSelection()` destroys the numeral, invokes `onSelect` and stops the
  scene. Public accessors already exist: `getCountdownText()`,
  `isCountdownActive()`, `isChoiceScreenVisible()`, `getOverlayElapsedMs()`.
- `src/scenes/core/holdFullCountdown.ts` owns the pure 3-2-1 scheduler
  (`HOLD_FULL_COUNTDOWN_COUNTS = 3`, `HOLD_FULL_COUNTDOWN_DURATION_MS`).
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts` uses its own `demoDwellMs ?? HANGAR_WAR_TRAVERSAL_DWELL_MS`
  for demo reward overlays, so it does not depend on the bot choice constant.
- Docs pin the current 900 ms pace: `README.md` (attract/demo paragraph) and
  `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 ("**900 ms**") and §4.5 (countdown tears
  the choice screen down, "leaving only the countdown numeral").
- Tests reference the constant symbolically (`BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS`), so
  a value change flows through `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` and
  `src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts` waits without hard-coded numbers.

## Desired change

1. Raise the demo dwell to 2500 ms (`BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS`), keeping the
   mini-boss wheel's demo spin delay at its current pace via a separate constant
   so only the upgrade-selection pause slows.
2. In `MineralChoiceScene`, render the chosen option's title beneath the
   countdown numeral when a selection starts the countdown, expose it for tests
   (e.g. `getCountdownTitle()`), and destroy it alongside the numeral in
   `completeSelection()` (and defensively on shutdown).
3. Update the overlay's module doc comment, README and GDD to describe the
   2.5 s bot dwell and the title-under-countdown readout.
4. Cover the above with unit tests and keep the demo integration and gym-parity
   suites green.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts` — raise `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS` to 2500 and
  (if the wheel is scoped out) add a separate demo-spin delay constant; update
  the doc comment.
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — new countdown-title text object + layout
  constant, title creation in `select()`, destruction in `completeSelection()`
  and shutdown, `getCountdownTitle()` accessor, module doc comment.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — hold-full/mini-boss-fallback `autoSelectMs` wiring
  and the wheel `autoSpinMs` constant separation (comments mention the new
  pace).
- `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts` — title-visible/title-cleared
  and 2500 ms dwell tests.
- `src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts` — assert the selected title under
  the countdown on the demo path.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — only where the wheel/choice delay is asserted.
- `README.md` — attract/demo paragraph: 2.5 s dwell + selected title.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.4 auto-select bullet, §4.5 countdown
  bullet.

## Related work

- AH-0MUXXQ1MN002RXGB — *Demo bot: human-like input limits and complete the
  hold-full upgrade choice* (completed): introduced the demo auto-select and
  `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS`.
- AH-0MV55OBKS006TL4N — *Demo/attract auto-select routes through the countdown*
  (completed): the bot's auto-select must drive the same selection → 3-2-1 →
  on-beat resume path.
- AH-0MV55OAQT004NMSN — *Beat-locked 3-2-1 countdown and on-beat resume*
  (completed): owns the countdown scheduler and the "numeral only" teardown this
  item extends with the chosen title.
- AH-0MVJ8U79V0056I2F — *AI bot does not know how to select upgrade in
  mini-boss reward screen* (completed): the mini-boss reward auto-select and
  wheel spin sharing the same demo delay.
- AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q — *Asteroids drop collectable minerals that fill the
  ship's hold and grant a power-up choice* (completed): the hold-full overlay
  itself.
- AH-0MV722WJS0075UTZ — countdown teardown of the choice UI (the behaviour the
  title readout complements).
- AH-0MV03GXZQ00801T4 / AH-0MW3MLV2V001NWBR — the retired Extra Life
  auto-select preference; the auto-select always takes option 0 today.

### Related work (automated report)

- **AH-0MVH80ZJ7009W18Z** – Some power-ups appear to do nothing (completed)
- **AH-0MV55OBKS006TL4N** – Demo/attract auto-select routes through the
  countdown (completed)
- **AH-0MVD20MYX0028JFL** – Close coverage gap: AC2 upgrade choices simulated
  (completed)

### Potentially related docs

- `README.md` (attract/demo mode paragraph) — documents the current 900 ms
  auto-select and the countdown/resume cadence.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 (bot) and §4.5 (hold-full overlay) —
  the two canonical descriptions of this behaviour.
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` — demo capture expectations that exercise the
  overlay.

## Assumptions and decisions for producer confirmation

- **A1 — Dwell scope.** The 2.5 s pause applies to the **upgrade selection
  overlay** only (hold-full choice, and the hold-full-style mini-boss
  fallback, which reuse `MineralChoiceScene`). The **mini-boss reward wheel**
  keeps its current demo auto-spin pace (split into its own constant), because
  the item describes an upgrade *selection* screen; the wheel has no selection
  and no titled options. *If the producer wants every bot reward overlay
  slowed to 2.5 s, AC4 is simply dropped and the wheel keeps the shared
  constant.*
- **A2 — Title scope.** The chosen title is shown for **every** selection on the
  shared overlay (bot auto-select and human), not bot-only: the choice UI is
  torn down for both, so the readout is equally useful and there is no penalty
  in normal play. *If bot-only is wanted, gate the title on the demo flag.*
- **A3 — Title copy.** The "title" is the option's catalogue `name` (e.g.
  `Spread Shot Lv.3`), i.e. the same text the option label carried (without the
  `1.` prefix), not the change summary or description.
- **A4 — Countdown timing unchanged.** The 3-2-1 countdown stays three beats
  (2250 ms at 80 BPM) and still applies the choice on the beat after "1".
- **A5 — Title lifetime.** The title clears when the countdown completes (the
  overlay closes); it is not carried into gameplay or the HUD.

## Risks

- **Scope creep** — "make the demo's pacing nicer" invites unrelated overlay
  restyling; anything beyond the dwell + title readout becomes a linked
  follow-up item, not this item.
- **Timing fragility** — lengthening the dwell changes total overlay duration
  (2500 + 2250 ms); integration tests that wait on constants remain valid, but
  any test with a hard-coded wait must move to `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS`
  arithmetic.
- **Shared overlay regression** — the title must be torn down with the numeral
  in every exit path (completion, scene shutdown, scene restart) or a stale
  text object can leak between hold-fulls.
- **Wheel coupling** — `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS` currently feeds the
  wheel's `autoSpinMs`; splitting it is the only way to keep AC4 true, so the
  split must be explicit and documented.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should the 2.5 s pause apply to every bot reward overlay (hold-full
  choice, mini-boss wheel spin, hex-map demo reward overlays) or only the
  upgrade selection screen?"
  — Answer (agent, assumption A1, producer confirmation invited): only the
  upgrade selection overlay; the mini-boss wheel keeps its current delay via a
  separate constant. Source: work-item seed description ("the upgrade selection
  screen", "select whichever one they want") + repo inspection of
  `PlayScene.openMineralChoice` / `openMiniBossReward` / `HexMapScene`.
- Q: "Should the chosen title appear under the countdown for human selections
  too, or only for the bot?"
  — Answer (agent, assumption A2, producer confirmation invited): every
  selection on the shared overlay, because `select()` tears down the choice UI
  for both paths so the readout costs normal play nothing. Source: repo
  inspection of `MineralChoiceScene.select()` / `completeSelection()`.
- Q: "What is the 'title' — the option name, its change summary, or its
  description?"
  — Answer (agent, assumption A3): the catalogue option `name` (e.g.
  `Spread Shot Lv.3`), matching the label the option row showed. Source: seed
  wording "selected item's title" + `ChoiceOption` shape in
  `src/powerups/choice.ts`.
- Q: "Does the 3-2-1 countdown itself change length?"
  — Answer (agent, assumption A4): no — it stays beat-locked at three counts
  (2250 ms at the default 80 BPM) with the choice applied on the beat after
  "1". Source: `src/scenes/core/holdFullCountdown.ts` and
  AH-0MV55OAQT004NMSN.
- Q: "Which docs pin the current 900 ms pace?"
  — Answer (agent research): `README.md` attract/demo paragraph and
  `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 ("**900 ms**") and §4.5 (countdown
  "leaving only the countdown numeral"). Both need updating.

# When starting a Hex War battle, show the ship config screen

## Problem statement

A Hex War (Hangar War) battle can currently be started **without ever seeing
the ship-configuration screen**: activating an unheld hex on the hex map calls
`HexMapScene.deploy()`, which starts `PlayScene` directly (`src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts`,
`deploy()`). The player therefore commits a life with whatever loadout is
already equipped, and the boss's authored **strengths / weaknesses** — the
strategic intel the design promises ("the weapon that is strong against the
boss", `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` § *Known-ahead intel*) — are not visible
where the loadout is actually chosen.

This item makes the **hangar screen the pre-battle config screen on the way
into a hex** (the design of record calls it "a deployment / hull-and-loadout
selector on the way into a hex", `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md:1058`), and
makes that screen **target-aware**: it names the boss of the hex being attacked,
prints its strengths and weaknesses, and marks the player's weapons **green when
they counter that boss** and **red when the boss resists them**.

## Users

- **The strategist** — "I read that this boss is weak to `waveLaser`; when I
  pick the hex I want the config screen to tell me to bring it, and to warn me
  off the weapons the boss resists."
- **The grinder** — "I want the pre-battle screen to make a wrong loadout
  legible *before* I spend a life, not after three boss phases."
- **The accessibility-minded player** — "I must be able to read weapon
  effectiveness without relying on colour alone." (Repo CVD policy: never
  colour-only.)
- **The producer/maintainer** — "One shared model and renderer, so the game and
  `GymHangar` show the same screen and no scene owns a second matchup rule."

Example user stories:

- As a player, I select a hex on the map and land on the hangar/config screen
  for **that** hex before the fight starts.
- As a player, I see the target boss and its strengths and weaknesses on the
  config screen.
- As a player, I see which of my weapons are strong (green) and weak (red)
  against this boss, with a non-colour marker too.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **The ship config screen comes before a hex battle.** Activating an unheld
   hex on the hex map opens the ship-config (hangar) screen pre-targeted at that
   hex and does **not** start `PlayScene` directly. That screen's `▶ DEPLOY`
   row names the target hex and launches the deployment at it. Entering the
   hangar from the menu (no chosen hex) targets the existing default (the
   weakest unheld hex via `selectDeploymentHex`), so no hex battle begins
   without the config screen first.
2. **The target boss's intel is shown.** The config screen publishes the target
   hex's boss name and its authored `strengths` and `weaknesses` lists in a
   clearly labelled section, resolved from the shared ring definitions
   (`src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts`) — never a scene-local copy. An
   unauthored/unknown hex renders an explicit "unknown" fallback instead of
   throwing.
3. **Weapons are marked for the matchup.** Every weapon row the screen presents
   for the target — the `LOADOUT` starting-weapon selector **and** the unlock
   tree's weapon entries — carries its matchup against that boss's lists: a
   weapon in the boss's `weaknesses` (it counters the boss) is **strong** →
   green; a weapon in the boss's `strengths` (the boss resists it) is **weak**
   → red; every other weapon is **neutral**. Matchup resolution normalises the
   ring-data alias (`waveLaser` ↔ catalogue `wave_laser`) through the shared
   mapping the capture cycle already owns, so a catalogue weapon and an
   authored list can never disagree.
4. **Accessible and unambiguous, not colour-only.** Each strong/weak state also
   carries a non-colour marker (a glyph plus text tag, e.g. `▲ EFFECTIVE` /
   `▼ RESISTED`) so the matchup is readable without colour, per the repo's CVD
   policy; the highlight is visually distinguishable from the existing
   actionable (green) and disabled (muted) row colours.
5. **One shared code path (gym↔game parity).** The intel and the matchup live
   in the pure model (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts`) so `GymHangar`
   renders the identical screen read-only. The attract/demo traversal traverses
   the new config step (`map → config → deployment`) without stalling and
   within its existing action bound.
6. **Automated tests cover the feature.** A pure matchup resolver
   (`strong`/`weak`/`neutral`, including the `waveLaser`↔`wave_laser` alias);
   the model's boss-intel and per-row matchup fields; the map→config routing
   and target carry-through; `▶ DEPLOY` launching at the target hex; the
   unknown-hex fallback; and `GymHangar` parity of the shared model.
7. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes**, including
   code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Impact

Before every hex battle the player configures the ship on the hangar screen with
the target boss's strengths and weaknesses in view and their weapons marked
green or red for whether they counter or bounce off that boss — so a loadout is
a deliberate counter-pick, not a blind guess.

## Assumptions (documented; producer may override at review)

- **A1 — "ship config screen" means the existing hangar screen.** Reuse
  `HangarScene` / `buildHangarScreenModel` / `renderHangarScreen`; do not build
  a second config screen or a forked model.
- **A2 — "strong / weak" is player-centric.** A weapon the boss is **weak
  against** is strong (green); a weapon the boss is **strong against** is weak
  (red). This follows the design's "the weapon that is strong against the boss"
  language.
- **A3 — Highlight scope.** The highlight applies to every weapon row the
  screen presents for the target (the `LOADOUT` selector and the unlock tree's
  weapon entries); non-weapon rows keep their existing rendering.
- **A4 — Default target.** With no explicitly chosen hex (menu entry), the
  screen shows the intel of the deployment it would actually launch, i.e. the
  weakest unheld hex.
- **A5 — Transient target.** The target hex is launch data only; nothing new is
  persisted and the payload schema is unchanged.
- **A6 — CVD.** Green/red is always paired with a non-colour marker.
- **A7 — Display/flow only.** This item does **not** make the lists change the
  fight; that is AH-0MWL5376H001WJFZ.

## Constraints

- **Pure model, shared renderer.** Intel and matchup are computed in the pure
  screen model from shared data; the scene only presents and persists. Both the
  game and `GymHangar` consume the same model/renderer (AGENTS.md gym↔game
  parity, `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`).
- **Reuse the shared weapon-id alias.** Ring data spells the laser
  `waveLaser`; the catalogue spells it `wave_laser`. Match through the existing
  `GRANT_ALIASES` / `resolveHexGrant` mapping (`src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts`),
  never a second ad-hoc table.
- **Never colour-only** (CVD policy precedent in `src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts`).
- **No arcade-path change.** `PlayScene`, the arcade checkpoint, the leaderboard
  and the feature-flag entry surface are untouched; a hex deployment stays a
  separate session (no checkpoint write/clear).
- **No purchase/combat-rule change.** Prices, ownership, gating and the run's
  hit model are unchanged; this item changes what the config screen **shows**
  and when it is reached.
- **No stall in attract/demo.** The bot must traverse the added config step and
  remain bounded by `HANGAR_WAR_TRAVERSAL_MAX_ACTIONS`.
- **Layout safety.** The new intel section must not collide with the existing
  rows; keep the shared layout constants single-sourced.
- **Scope-creep risk.** A counter-weapon auto-pick, damage-type combat effects,
  in-combat effectiveness glyphs, or reshaping the unlock-tree economy are out
  of scope; record them as linked work items rather than expanding this one.

## Existing state

- **The map deploys directly.** `HexMapScene.deploy(hexId)`
  (`src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts`) builds the deployment and `scene.start`s
  `PlayScene`; the map's hex activation calls it. The map's own detail panel
  already publishes `STRENGTHS:` / `WEAKNESSES:` (via `buildHexMapModel`,
  `src/core/hangarWar/hexIntel.ts`) but has no loadout control.
- **The hangar already is a config screen, but not target-aware.** `HangarScene`
  renders the unlock tree plus the hull / starting-weapon / modifier selectors
  and the `▶ DEPLOY` row through `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts`. Its
  `deploy()` targets whatever `buildHangarDeployment` selects (explicit `hexId`
  or the weakest unheld hex); it accepts no target from launch data and shows
  no boss intel.
- **Boss strengths/weaknesses are authored data.** `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts`
  authors `boss`, `strengths` (weapons the boss resists, e.g. `['cannon','dual']`)
  and `weaknesses` (weapons that counter it, e.g. `['nova','arc']`) per hex.
  `resolveHexGrant` + `GRANT_ALIASES` normalise the ring/grant spelling to
  catalogue ids.
- **The catalogue's weapons** are `spread`, `wave_laser`, `ricochet`, `cluster`
  (plus grant-only/other entries), keyed by `id`; a hangar weapon option's `id`
  is a catalogue id, while boss lists carry shipped `WeaponId` spellings.
- **Parity gym.** `GymHangar` renders `buildHangarScreenModel` /
  `renderHangarScreen` read-only; any new model field automatically reaches it
  but must also be asserted there.

## Desired change

- **Route the map into the config screen.** `HexMapScene`'s hex activation opens
  `HangarScene` carrying `{ payload, storage, demo, demoDwellMs, targetHexId }`
  instead of starting `PlayScene`.
- **Make the hangar target-aware.** `HangarScene` accepts an optional
  `targetHexId` in launch data, threads it into `buildHangarScreenModel` and
  into `deploy()` so `▶ DEPLOY` launches at the chosen hex (default: weakest
  unheld hex).
- **Add the boss-intel section to the pure model.** Extend
  `buildHangarScreenModel` with the target hex's boss, strengths and weaknesses
  (resolved from the shared definitions), plus a per-weapon-row `matchup`
  verdict (`strong` | `weak` | `neutral`) for the `LOADOUT` selector and the
  unlock tree's weapon entries.
- **Add one pure matchup resolver** beside the ring/capture helpers: given a
  weapon id (catalogue or shipped spelling) and a hex definition, return
  `strong` / `weak` / `neutral`, normalising through the shared alias map.
- **Render it.** Extend `renderHangarScreen` to draw the intel section and to
  colour/mark weapon rows (green `▲ EFFECTIVE`, red `▼ RESISTED`, neutral
  unchanged), without colliding with the existing rows.
- **Traverse it in the demo.** Keep the attract traversal total: the map's
  "deploy at hex" step now lands on the config screen, whose own decision
  buys or deploys at the carried target.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts` — boss-intel section, per-row matchup
  verdict, coloured/glyphed rendering, target-aware DEPLOY.
- `src/scenes/HangarScene.ts` — accept `targetHexId`, thread into the model and
  `deploy()`.
- `src/scenes/HexMapScene.ts` — route hex activation to the config screen with
  the target hex.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexRing.ts` / `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` — shared
  definitions source (read-only).
- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` — reuse `GRANT_ALIASES` /
  `resolveHexGrant` for spelling normalisation (or extract the alias lookup).
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts` — target-hex resolution
  (`selectDeploymentHex`) reuse.
- `src/ai/hangarWarTraversal.ts` — demo routing through the config step.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.ts` — parity of the new model/render.
- Tests: `src/scenes/HangarScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/HexMapScene.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.test.ts`, plus new pure-model/matchup tests.

## Related work

- **AH-0MWL5376H001WJFZ — Make hex strengths and weaknesses matter in combat**
  (open): the mechanical effect of the same lists. This item is the
  **display/flow** half; they share the `strong`/`weak` vocabulary and the
  alias normalisation, but neither duplicates the other's rules.
- **AH-0MVU3VNJI00066YE — Build Candidate D — Hangar War (outer loop)**
  (completed): the design of record, including "a deployment / hull-and-loadout
  selector on the way into a hex".
- **AH-0MVUXC1X6007KAG1 — Hangar scene: unlock tree and deployment/loadout
  selector** (completed): the screen and model this item extends.
- **AH-0MVUXCAG90086LH2 — Hex map scene with known-ahead intel** (completed):
  the map that already publishes boss strengths/weaknesses and the target rule.
- **AH-0MVUXC2DD003HN0I — Hangar War menu entry, mode separation and deployment**
  (completed): the `▶ DEPLOY` / deployment-payload path.
- **AH-0MWL8C6FE008G1E7 — Saved ship configurations** (open): adjacent loadout
  UX; no overlap with this item's intel/highlight goal.
- Automated find-related report also surfaced: AH-0MUE2MGM0001XEH9 (CSV seed
  data), AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D (deployments start with the default weapon only),
  AH-0MWHWF5D4000J0RB (held-hex UPGRADE DEFENCES, blocked).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**No producer interview was required.** The seed context plus the design of
record (`docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` § *UI / scene surface* and §
*Known-ahead intel*, GDD §8.2) were sufficient to draft a clear brief. The
interpretive decisions below are recorded as **documented assumptions** (see
*Assumptions* above); the producer may override any of them at review without
gating the brief.

- **Q1 — Which screen is the "ship config screen"?**
  Answer (agent, documented assumption A1): the existing hangar screen
  (`HangarScene` + `buildHangarScreenModel`/`renderHangarScreen`). Evidence:
  `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md:1058` names "a deployment / hull-and-loadout
  selector on the way into a hex", and `hangarScreen.ts`'s own header calls it
  the deployment/hull-and-loadout selector.
- **Q2 — "Strong/weak" from whose perspective?**
  Answer (agent, documented assumption A2): player-centric — boss `weaknesses`
  = weapons that counter it → green; boss `strengths` = weapons it resists →
  red. Evidence: the design's "the weapon that is strong against the boss"
  (`docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` § *Known-ahead intel*; GDD §8.2 "Boss and
  weapon strength are known ahead").
- **Q3 — Which weapon rows are highlighted?**
  Answer (agent, documented assumption A3): every weapon row shown for the
  target — the `LOADOUT` starting-weapon selector and the unlock tree's weapon
  entries. Non-weapon rows unchanged.
- **Q4 — Normalisation of ring vs catalogue weapon ids?**
  Answer: reuse the shared `GRANT_ALIASES` / `resolveHexGrant` mapping
  (`waveLaser` ↔ `wave_laser`); no second alias table. Evidence: the related
  item AH-0MWL5376H001WJFZ Q5 fixed this same normalisation.
- **Q5 — Colour-only signalling?**
  Answer: no — pair green/red with a non-colour glyph/tag, per the repo CVD
  policy (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hexMap.ts`).

# Reconcile arena moving-hostile profiles with the class models and fix the chaser over-dodge

**Raised by:** AH-0MWM0C5BN003PCDT (seeded per-class avoidance sweep).
**Blocks:** AH-0MWM0C5BN003PCDT — the sweep cannot satisfy its pass bar until this lands.
**Priority:** high (epic AH-0MWLUIOH9001XBJ3 acceptance evidence).

## Problem

The seeded per-class sweep over the headless arena (Feature 6's moving-hostile
opt-in, live competent brain, `hazardMotionModelEnabled` on/off, 12 seeds,
1800 ticks, 4 immortal single-class bodies, 2 minerals) measures **avoidable**
enemy-body contacts (a contact is avoidable when a 16-direction escape fan at
`playerSpeed` clears the contact radius from the body's fitted velocity 0.25 s
before the overlap). Measured with the arena's shipped class profiles:

| class | contacts off | contacts on | seeds better / worse / tie | aggregate off→on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| chaser | 46 | 39 | 5 / 0 / 7 | −15% |
| diver | 79 | 47 | 9 / 0 / 3 | −41% |
| patroller | 19 | 21 | 4 / 4 / 4 | +11% |
| formation (control) | 10 | 26 | 1 / 5 / 6 | +160% |
| roamer (control) | 22 | 20 | 2 / 1 / 9 | −9% |

The AC's bar (curving classes strictly fewer on a **majority** of seeds;
`roamer`/`formation` **never increase**) is therefore not met: `chaser` reduces
but only on 5/12 seeds, `patroller` is flat, and both controls increase on some
seeds. The 60 Hz scripted-curving proof in
`src/ai/botSteering.integration.test.ts` (off: min distance 25.7 px, inside the
30 px contact radius; on: 39.2 px, clear) shows the model *does* work when the
scripted trajectory matches the class model — so the failure is in the harness /
live closed-loop interaction, not in the sampler's core idea.

## Diagnosis

1. **Harness and predictor disagree about the class semantics.** Feature 6's
   arena profiles are a sinusoidal `patroller` weave and a circular `formation`
   sway (`hostileMotionVelocity`), while the predictor's class models are
   `patroller` = straight patrol then straight commit and `formation` = linear
   drift + edge reflection (`src/ai/framework/hazardMotionModel.ts`). The sweep
   is validating each predictor against a trajectory it does not model.
   Re-running with the arena profile temporarily changed to the predictor's
   semantics made both classes neutral-to-better (patroller aggregate 58→51,
   89→81; formation 23→19, 13→12), confirming the mismatch.
2. **The chaser over-dodges.** With the model on, a pursuing chaser is predicted
   to threaten every bearing; `planSteering` picks the least-bad escape, which
   keeps the ship near the body, and rising-edge contacts increase (the control
   arm flies its line and often finishes with one contact per body). This is the
   behaviour the pinned note in `hazardMotionModel.test.ts` warned about.
3. **The metric is coarse.** With 4 immortal bodies, contacts saturate at one
   per body, so per-seed comparisons are dominated by ties. Any fix should
   either raise the encounter rate (fast crossing geometry) or measure at a
   finer granularity while keeping the AC's per-seed rule.

## Acceptance criteria

- The arena's moving-hostile class profiles and the predictor's class models
  describe the **same** trajectory semantics, asserted by a test (a class
  profile the predictor does not model must fail that test).
- The chaser sweep arm no longer regresses: a live competent bot with the
  motion model on records **no more** avoidable contacts than the
  constant-velocity control on any seed, and strictly fewer on a majority.
- The seeded per-class sweep (`src/ai/eval/hazardMotionSweep.test.ts`) lands
  green with the AC bar: `chaser`/`diver`/`patroller` strictly fewer avoidable
  contacts on a majority of a documented seed list; `roamer`/`formation` never
  increase. A failure names the offending seed and class.
- With that evidence, flip `COMPETENT_BOT_TUNABLES.hazardMotionModelEnabled` to
  `true`, update the pin in `hazardMotionModel.test.ts` (with the evidence
  reference, not silently), and re-baseline any eval expectation the flip
  genuinely moves, recording the rationale.

## Evidence / artefacts

- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` — the moving mode now exposes each hostile's stable
  `id`/`movementClass` on the bot snapshot (only under the opt-in), which the
  tracker needs to fit a velocity at all.
- `src/ai/botSteering.integration.test.ts` — the 60 Hz scripted-curving proof.
- Measurement harness and per-seed numbers reproducible from the described
  scenario (recorded on AH-0MWM0C5BN003PCDT).

**Key files:** `src/ai/eval/arena.ts`, `src/ai/framework/hazardMotionModel.ts`,
`src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts`, `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts`,
`src/ai/eval/hazardMotionSweep.test.ts` (new), `src/ai/eval/arena.test.ts`.

# Intake Brief — Automatically select strong weapons (AH-0MWOROJYT004WPSD)

> **Status:** draft produced without an interactive producer (the item was
> auto-dispatched by the herdr downtime worker). The scope below is derived from
> the operator's seed intent and from the code/design docs. Three scope
> decisions are recorded as **OPEN QUESTION**s in the Appendix and the item is
> flagged for producer review; the draft applies the recommended default so
> planning is not blocked.

## Problem statement

The target-aware hangar (config) screen already shows the chosen hex boss's
intel and marks every weapon row `▲ EFFECTIVE` (green) / `▼ RESISTED` (red),
but the loadout itself is left entirely to the player: a fresh deployment
carries an **empty** starting-weapon selection, and a returning player may carry
a stale mix that ignores the upcoming boss, so the recorded intel does not
change what the fleet actually flies with. The ask is to make the screen choose
a sensible default — automatically equip the owned weapons that are **strong**
against the target boss, then fill the remaining loadout capacity with a
balanced variety of weapons/power-ups — and to colour the equipped list green
(strong) and red (weak).

## Users

- **Player arriving at a hex** — wants the strongest sensible kit selected for
  them so a hex battle does not begin under-equipped or with a stale loadout.
  - *As a player, when I open the hangar for a hex whose boss the Wave Laser
    counters, I want the Wave Laser already equipped, so I do not have to
    re-derive the intel myself.*
  - *As a player, I want the remaining slots filled with a varied, useful mix
    rather than one family stacked to the cap.*
- **Player who customises** — wants their deliberate choice to survive; an
  automatic selection must not silently undo a hand-picked loadout every time
  the screen reopens. *(See Appendix Q1 — this is the key open decision.)*
- **Producer/designer** — wants one shared, pure selection rule consumed by the
  game and `GymHangar`, so no scene owns a second loadout policy and the
  gym↔game parity rule holds.
- **Maintainer** — wants the selection to reuse the shipped six-slot cap and
  the shipped matchup resolver (`resolveBossMatchup`) rather than introduce a
  second power/strength model.

## Existing state (verified in code)

- **Matchup display already exists.** `resolveBossMatchup(weaponId, definition)`
  (`src/core/hangarWar/weaponMatchup.ts`) returns `'strong' | 'weak' |
  'neutral'`; `buildHangarWeaponOptions` marks each weapon row with
  `withMatchupMarker` and `rowColour` applies `HANGAR_STRONG_COLOR` /
  `HANGAR_WEAK_COLOR` (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts`). The colouring
  part of the seed intent appears **already satisfied for weapon rows**; the
  open question is whether power-ups/equipped items need it too, given only
  weapons have a boss matchup.
- **The default loadout is deliberately empty.** GDD § *Hangar economy and
  unlock tree* and AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D: `activeLoadout.startingWeapons: []`,
  and "owning the free starter weapon never auto-equips it — equipping a
  starter is always a deliberate choice". This item proposes to change that
  default for the pre-battle case, so the design-of-record wording must be
  updated.
- **A purchase auto-equips.** `purchaseHangarEntry` buys with
  `equipOnPurchase: true`, so bought parts already land owned-and-armed. This
  is a different mechanism from the requested automatic selection.
- **Six shared loadout slots.** `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP = 6`
  (`src/core/constants.ts`); weapons and power-ups share the cap.
  `applyHangarWarDeployment` (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts`) trims
  the combined list (selected weapons first, then owned power-up levels)
  through `capDropIdsToSlotPool` before granting, so an over-full loadout is
  already trimmed silently — the screen can show more selected weapons than the
  run actually carries (AH-0MVVF0POV001JNKX).
- **Power-ups are not loadout-selectable.** Every owned level-bearing power-up
  is granted on deployment (`levels.powerUps`); the hangar loadout model
  (`HangarLoadout`) has only `startingWeapons` and `modifiers`. So "select
  power-ups to fill slots" does not map to an existing selection surface — see
  Appendix Q2.
- **Every deployment has a target hex.** The hangar screen accepts an optional
  `targetHexId` (set when the map opens it via `HexMapScene.openConfig`); with
  none, `selectDeploymentHex` still resolves the weakest unheld hex, so the
  screen almost always has a boss to fit against.
- **No auto-selection exists today.** There is no "auto-equip"/"auto-fit"
  function, no "the player customised this loadout" flag, and no balancing
  rule for a > cap owned set.

## Desired change (proposed — subject to the Appendix answers)

1. Add a **pure auto-loadout selector** that, given the payload, the target hex
   definition and the catalogue, returns a starting-weapon selection:
   - include every owned weapon whose matchup is `strong` against the boss;
   - exclude `weak` weapons;
   - fill the remaining capacity with `neutral` owned weapons/power-ups, chosen
     for **variety** (not all one family) up to the shared six-slot cap, leaving
     room for the owned power-ups that will also consume slots at grant time.
2. Apply the selector when the hangar screen is shown **ahead of a battle**
   (target hex resolved), according to the trigger/override policy settled by
   Appendix Q1.
3. Keep the manual toggles working after auto-selection, and keep the six-slot
   display honest (the selected list should not claim more slots than the run
   will grant).
4. Ensure the equipped list colours strong (green) / weak (red) with a
   non-colour glyph tag (CVD policy), and confirm the gym renders the same model
   read-only (gym↔game parity).
5. Update the design-of-record wording (GDD § Hangar economy and unlock tree,
   `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, module JSDoc) to state the new automatic-selection
   rule and its override policy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Strong weapons are auto-equipped.** Opening the hangar screen
      ahead of a battle on a hex whose authored `weaknesses` name an owned
      weapon selects that weapon in `activeLoadout.startingWeapons` (via
      `resolveBossMatchup === 'strong'`), pinned by a pure selector test.
- [ ] **AC2 — Weak weapons are not auto-selected.** An owned weapon whose
      matchup is `weak` is never added by the auto-selector, and is not forced
      into the selection by the fill step.
- [ ] **AC3 — The selection fills the available capacity with variety.** The
      selector fills toward the shared six-slot cap (`POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP`)
      without exceeding it, accounts for the owned power-ups that will also
      consume slots at grant time, and applies a documented variety rule
      (Appendix Q3) so the result is not a single family stacked to the cap.
- [ ] **AC4 — Manual control is preserved.** After auto-selection the player can
      still toggle any owned weapon; the override policy settled by Appendix Q1
      is implemented and pinned (a deliberate choice is not silently undone if
      the producer chooses the "preserve manual" option).
- [ ] **AC5 — Equipped list colour semantics.** The equipped/loadout list
      colours strong rows green and weak rows red, always paired with a
      non-colour glyph tag (never colour-only, repo CVD policy), and rows with
      no matchup verdict stay neutral. The gym renders the identical model.
- [ ] **AC6 — One shared, pure rule.** The selector is pure and Phaser-free,
      lives in the shared core/model (not scene code), is consumed by the game
      and `GymHangar`, and reuses `resolveBossMatchup`, the shipped catalogue
      and the shared slot-cap helper — no second matchup or slot rule.
- [ ] **AC7 — Determinism and idempotence.** The selector is deterministic for
      a given (payload, target, catalogue) — no wall-clock, no unseeded draws —
      and re-applying it does not duplicate entries or oscillate the selection.
- [ ] **AC8 — Automated tests cover every behaviour above**, and the
      changed-scope test gate passes.
- [ ] **AC9 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect
      the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or
      docs site entries (GDD § Hangar economy and unlock tree,
      `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, module JSDoc).
- [ ] **AC10 — Full project test suite.** Full project test suite must pass with
      the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md).** The selection rule must be consumed by the
  game and every gym that renders the hangar screen; `GymHangar` renders the
  same model read-only. No per-scene copy.
- **Reuse the shipped rules.** Matchup verdicts come from
  `resolveBossMatchup`; slot accounting from `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP` /
  `capDropIdsToSlotPool`; ownership from the pure economy. No new power model.
- **CVD policy.** Colour is never the only signal — the `▲ EFFECTIVE` /
  `▼ RESISTED` glyph tag stays primary.
- **No silent divergence from the six-slot cap.** The selected loadout must
  never present more counted kinds than the run will grant.
- **Determinism.** No wall-clock or unseeded randomness.
- **Scope guard.** Do not re-tune weapon balance, change the matchup resolver,
  or redesign the unlock tree here; those are separate items. Do not widen into
  the combat-effects of strengths/weaknesses (AH-0MWL5376H001WJFZ).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/hangarWar/weaponMatchup.ts` — reuse `resolveBossMatchup` (read-only).
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts` — the model builder and the
  loadout/equipped-list rendering; where the auto-selection is presented and
  applied.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` — owned-entry resolution and loadout
  helpers; the new pure selector likely lives in or beside this module.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts` — the six-slot grant trim the
  selector must agree with.
- `src/powerups/slots.ts` — `capDropIdsToSlotPool` / `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP`
  (read-only).
- `src/scenes/HangarScene.ts` — applies the selection and persists the payload.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.ts` — read-only parity render.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/*.test.ts`, `src/core/hangarWar/*.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.test.ts` — pure-selector and render tests.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — § Hangar economy and unlock tree
  (default-empty wording).
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — parity matrix note.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — overwriting a deliberate loadout.** If auto-selection runs and
  persists on every screen open, a player's hand-picked loadout is lost on each
  visit. Mitigation: settle the override policy (Appendix Q1); the recommended
  default applies auto-selection only when the loadout is at its default/empty,
  or exposes it as an explicit action, rather than clobbering a custom set.
- **Risk — power-ups are not selectable.** "Select power-ups to fill slots" may
  imply a new selection surface. Mitigation: Appendix Q2 distinguishes
  "budget for auto-granted power-ups" (small) from "add power-up loadout
  selection" (large, likely a separate item).
- **Risk — vague "balanced variety".** Without a weapon taxonomy, "balanced"
  is undefined. Mitigation: Appendix Q3 offers concrete rules; the recommended
  default is one-per-weapon-behaviour then round-robin by catalogue order.
- **Risk — colour-only meaning.** Mitigation: the glyph tag is mandatory (CVD).
- **Risk — scope creep.** Rebalancing weapons, changing the matchup rule, or by
  making strengths/weaknesses affect combat are separate items — record as
  linked work, not scope.
- **Assumption A1 — "strong" means `resolveBossMatchup === 'strong'`** (the
  existing display rule, player-centric: a weapon in the boss's `weaknesses`).
- **Assumption A2 — "slots" means the shared six-slot loadout cap.**
- **Assumption A3 — the colouring requirement is mostly shipped for weapon
  rows**; this item verifies/preserves it and extends it only where the
  equipped list is changed.
- **Assumption A4 — the automatic selection is a pre-battle default, not a
  mid-run rule**, so it belongs in the hangar model, not the combat core.

## Related work

- AH-0MWMT4NJV001PX8Y — Weapon-vs-boss matchup resolver (completed) — the
  `strong`/`weak` rule this item reuses.
- AH-0MWMT4QXF0095CBN — Target-aware config screen model and render
  (completed) — the intel block and per-row matchup marking.
- AH-0MWMT4STK001PSK4 — Gym parity and documentation (completed) — the
  gym↔game rendering contract.
- AH-0MWMT4S5U001EGDF — Hex map routes into the config screen (completed) —
  the `targetHexId` path that makes the screen "ahead of a battle".
- AH-0MWOQSV7P002IC5Y — Weak/Resist on hangar equip is misleading (open,
  plan_complete) — sibling: it suppresses the highlight on rows the player
  cannot act on; this item changes *what is selected*, not the highlight
  policy. Not a duplicate.
- AH-0MVVF0POV001JNKX — Loadout can exceed the six-slot cap (completed) — the
  cap and trim rule the selector must honour.
- AH-0MWCFKHWD002RKX9 — Hex War doesn't add initial loadout to slots
  (completed) — deployment → HUD grant path.
- AH-0MWB8VDU4007G1LQ — Model the per-ring deployment loadout (completed) —
  precedent for "equip every owned weapon (slot-capped)" as a modelled loadout;
  this item adds boss-aware selection to that idea.
- AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D — the default-empty loadout decision this item revises.
- AH-0MWL5376H001WJFZ — Make hex strengths and weaknesses matter in combat
  (open) — the mechanical matchup; out of scope here (display-only per
  AH-0MWMT4NJV001PX8Y assumption A7).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` § Hangar economy and unlock tree.
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`.
- `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D § Attract mode (auto-select).

## Impact

A player opening the hangar before a hex battle gets a loadout already fitted
to the boss — strong weapons equipped, weak ones left behind, remaining slots
usefully filled — so they can deploy with confidence instead of re-deriving the
intel by hand.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

> This intake was auto-dispatched by the herdr downtime worker, so no
> interactive producer was present. Questions are recorded here with the
> agent's recommended option and the assumption applied to the draft; each is
> also mirrored in a work-item comment. The item is flagged for producer review.

- **Q1 (OPEN QUESTION) — Trigger and override policy.** When should the
  automatic selection run, and what happens to a hand-picked loadout?
  - **A. Auto-fit on every open of the screen ahead of a battle**, persisting
    the result; manual toggles afterwards still work but are replaced next
    visit.
  - **B. Auto-fit only when the loadout is at its default/empty state** (the
    shipped default is empty), preserving any deliberate customisation.
  - **C. Auto-fit behind an explicit action** (e.g. an `AUTO-FIT` row/button)
    that the player invokes, leaving the default-empty rule intact otherwise.
  - **D. Auto-fit on open but do not persist** — present it as a transient
    recommendation until the player deploys or toggles.
  - **Recommended: B** — it delivers "automatically equipped" for the common
    (empty) case without silently discarding a deliberate loadout, and it is
    the smallest change to the design-of-record "equipping is deliberate"
    wording. *Not answered — no interactive producer. Draft assumes B.*

- **Q2 (OPEN QUESTION) — Do "power-ups" become loadout-selectable?** Today
  every owned level-bearing power-up is granted automatically on deployment and
  is not part of `HangarLoadout`; "select weapons/power-ups to fill slots"
  therefore has two readings:
  - **A. Budget only.** The selector accounts for the power-ups that will be
    auto-granted and fills the remaining slots with weapons, so power-ups are
    not crowded out. No new selection surface. *(Small.)*
  - **B. Add power-up selection.** Extend the loadout model and screen so the
    player (and the auto-selector) choose power-ups explicitly. *(Large — a new
    feature, likely its own item.)*
  - **Recommended: A** — it satisfies "fill as many slots as possible, picking
    a balanced variety" using the shipped grant model and avoids a second,
    much larger feature hiding inside a loadout-selection item.
    *Not answered — no interactive producer. Draft assumes A.*

- **Q3 (OPEN QUESTION) — What is "balanced variety"?** With no weapon taxonomy
  in the repo today:
  - **A.** At most one weapon per behaviour/pattern family (spread, beam,
    bounce, split, orbit, AoE), then fill remaining slots in catalogue order.
  - **B.** Round-robin across `strong` then `neutral` weapons in catalogue
    order, capped at N per family.
  - **C.** Prefer `strong` weapons, then include at least one defensive
    power-up, then fill with highest-permanent-level items.
  - **Recommended: A** — "variety" maps naturally to distinct weapon
    behaviours and is deterministic and easy to test; B/C can be layered later.
    *Not answered — no interactive producer. Draft assumes A.*

- **Q4 (RESOLVED by repo research) — Does the "colour strong/weak" requirement
  need new work?** The per-row matchup marker (`▲ EFFECTIVE` / `▼ RESISTED`)
  and the strong/weak row colours already ship in `hangarScreen.ts`
  (`withMatchupMarker`, `rowColour`, `HANGAR_STRONG_COLOR` /
  `HANGAR_WEAK_COLOR`). Only weapons carry a boss matchup, so power-up rows are
  neutral. This item preserves that behaviour and covers it with the equipped
  list it changes; no new colour rule is introduced unless the producer asks.
  *Source:* `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts`, `src/core/hangarWar/weaponMatchup.ts`,
  AH-0MWMT4QXF0095CBN / AH-0MWMT4STK001PSK4 (completed).

**Research summary:** Inspected `weaponMatchup.ts`, `hangarScreen.ts`
(`buildHangarScreenModel`, `buildHangarWeaponOptions`, `rowColour`),
`hangarDeployment.ts` (`buildHangarDeployment`, `applyHangarWarDeployment`,
six-slot trim), `hangarEconomy.ts` (`resolveActiveLoadout`), `types.ts`
(`HangarLoadout`), `slots.ts` (`POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP`, `capDropIdsToSlotPool`),
`HangarScene.ts`, `HexMapScene.ts` (`openConfig`), `hangarCatalogue.ts` and
`hexRingDefinitions.ts` (owned weapons/power-ups and ring grants);
`docs/Game Design Document.md` § Hangar economy and unlock tree (default-empty
loadout) and `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` Candidate D (attract auto-select).
Duplicate check run (`wl search` for auto-equip/strong weapons, loadout slots,
target intel matchup): the closest items are the completed matchup/intel work
and the open AH-0MWOQSV7P002IC5Y (highlight-on-non-actionable rows) — related,
not duplicates.

# Replace in-repo video processing with the `vidc` CLI

**Issue type:** task · **Priority:** high

## User story

As a maintainer, I want AI_Hell to stop owning its own FFmpeg video-processing
pipeline and instead delegate video compilation to the `vidc` CLI
(`video_compiler`), so that video processing has a single maintained home and
this repository contains only game, capture and telemetry code.

## Background

The repository's post-capture video processing lives in the promo compiler:
`scripts/compile-promo.mjs` (FFmpeg argv planning, per-junction
`xfade`/`acrossfade`, VP9/Opus encoding, probe + brightness + pace validation)
plus its pool inventory (`scripts/list-capture-pool.mjs`) and their tests and
docs. `vidc` (cloned at `../video_compiler`) is the replacement engine: it
discovers clips, orders them, probes with `ffprobe`, and renders one normalised
MP4 with a single FFmpeg invocation, supporting formats and render profiles.

Capture (Playwright `MediaRecorder` → WebM), the capture-time probe/seek/remux
helpers and the action-intensity series export are **capture tooling**, not the
post-capture video-processing pipeline, and stay.

## Decisions

- No backward compatibility: the bespoke compiler, its selection/validation
  logic, its manifests and its tests are deleted rather than kept beside vidc.
- Deliverables become MP4 (vidc's native output), replacing the legacy
  VP9/Opus WebM deliverables.
- Missing vidc capabilities surface during this migration are tracked in the
  `video_compiler` project as **high priority** items and synced:
  - `VC-0MWNOFIBI007J8UK` — render integration honours clip bounds
    (`source_range` in/out trimming).
  - `VC-0MWNW4SPX002J2SE` — transition-aware filter graph (per-junction
    `xfade`/`acrossfade`).
  - `VC-0MWNW4SYJ009XMIP` — compile/render transition hand-off.
  (The automated highlight selection is intentionally dropped with the legacy
  pipeline; vidc owns editing.)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `scripts/compile-promo.mjs` and its type/test files are removed, along
      with `scripts/list-capture-pool.mjs` and its type/test files.
- [ ] A new thin renderer (`scripts/render-promo.mjs`) forwards to
      `vidc render` (binary overridable via `--vidc` / `VIDC_BIN`), forwards
      subprocess output and exit code, supports `--dir`, `--output`,
      `--pattern`, `--format` (repeatable), `--fade-duration`, `--resolution`,
      `--fps`, `--overwrite`, `--dry-run`, `--json` and `--help`.
- [ ] The renderer is covered by unit tests (mocked subprocess) for argv
      forwarding, exit-code propagation, missing-binary remediation and
      `--json`/`--dry-run` passthrough.
- [ ] `package.json` drops the legacy `list:pool` entry and points
      `capture:promo` at the new renderer.
- [ ] The legacy video-processing documentation is removed: the
      "Pool inventory" and "Compiling a promo package" sections of
      `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, and the highlight-selection / pace-band
      sections (§7.5, §7.6) of `docs/dev/action-intensity.md`, with
      cross-references and `src/promoCompileDocs.test.ts` updated or removed.
- [ ] Doc guards that imported constants from the deleted compiler
      (`src/actionIntensityDocs.test.ts`, `scripts/promo-scenarios.test.ts`,
      `scripts/capture-scenarios.test.ts`) are updated to use the surviving
      editorial-category vocabulary.
- [ ] `npm run build` and the changed-scope test gate pass.

## Impact

Maintainers no longer carry a bespoke FFmpeg promo pipeline in AI_Hell: video
compilation is delegated to the maintained `vidc` CLI.

## Assumptions

- Capture recording, capture-time probing/remuxing and action-intensity series
  export are capture tooling, not the post-capture video-processing pipeline.
- MP4 is acceptable as the deliverable container for promos.
- Automated highlight selection is out of scope after the migration and is
  removed with the legacy compiler; vidc's timeline editing is the forward path
  once its trimming/transition items land.

## Key Files

- `scripts/compile-promo.mjs`, `scripts/compile-promo.d.mts`
- `scripts/compile-promo.test.ts`, `scripts/compile-promo.e2e.test.ts`
- `scripts/list-capture-pool.mjs`, `scripts/list-capture-pool.d.mts`, `scripts/list-capture-pool.test.ts`
- `scripts/render-promo.mjs`, `scripts/render-promo.d.mts`, `scripts/render-promo.test.ts`
- `package.json`
- `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, `docs/dev/action-intensity.md`, `README.md`
- `src/promoCompileDocs.test.ts`, `src/actionIntensityDocs.test.ts`
- `scripts/promo-scenarios.mjs`, `scripts/promo-scenarios.test.ts`
- `scripts/capture-scenarios.mjs`, `scripts/capture-scenarios.test.ts`, `scripts/capture-scenario-schema.mjs`

question: Intake needs three producer decisions before this brief can be finalised (full detail in the item description's Appendix):

**Q1 — Trigger & override policy.** When should the auto-fit run, and what happens to a hand-picked loadout?
- A. Auto-fit on every open ahead of a battle (persisted; manual changes replaced next visit).
- B. Auto-fit only when the loadout is at its default/empty state (preserve deliberate customisation).
- C. Auto-fit behind an explicit `AUTO-FIT` action (default-empty rule unchanged otherwise).
- D. Auto-fit on open but do not persist (transient recommendation until deploy/toggle).
**Recommended: B** — delivers "automatically equipped" for the common empty case without silently discarding a deliberate loadout.

**Q2 — Do power-ups become loadout-selectable?** Today every owned level-bearing power-up is auto-granted at deployment and is not part of `HangarLoadout`.
- A. Budget only: the selector accounts for auto-granted power-ups and fills remaining slots with weapons (no new selection surface).
- B. Add power-up selection: extend the loadout model and screen so the player/auto-selector choose power-ups explicitly (large, likely a separate item).
**Recommended: A** — satisfies "fill slots with a balanced variety" using the shipped grant model.

**Q3 — What is "balanced variety"?** (No weapon taxonomy exists today.)
- A. At most one weapon per behaviour family (spread/beam/bounce/split/orbit/AoE), then catalogue order.
- B. Round-robin across `strong` then `neutral` in catalogue order, cap N per family.
- C. Prefer `strong`, then at least one defensive power-up, then highest permanent level.
**Recommended: A** — "variety" maps to distinct weapon behaviours; deterministic and easy to test.

Colour note (resolved): the `▲ EFFECTIVE` / `▼ RESISTED` markers and strong/weak row colours already ship (`hangarScreen.ts` + `weaponMatchup.ts`); only weapons carry a boss matchup, so power-ups stay neutral. This item will preserve that behaviour.

Draft applies the recommended defaults so planning is not blocked. Please answer Q1–Q3 (or confirm the recommendations).
